title: Authorization Evidence Fusion and Warranty Process
author: Sofia Ruiz
body:
Overview

Purpose:
This document defines the Authorization Evidence Fusion (AEF) and Warranty Process: a standardized operational workflow and SLA matrix that ensures RBAC/authz decisions, audit logs, and residency/retention evidence are assembled, validated, and held under warranty for compliance reviews and incident forensics. The AEF process both (1) fuses telemetry from auth systems and audit logs into a single evidence bundle, and (2) creates a timebound warranty that guarantees evidence integrity and accessibility for a defined retention window.

Scope:
- Applies to all hosted, dedicated, and private (VPC/on-prem) Redwood Inference deployments.
- Covers evidence artifacts related to: authorization decisions, entitlement changes, service-to-service token issuance, privileged role activations, and audit events that materially affect multi-tenant isolation or data residency.
- Excludes raw application payload artifacts covered under data-residency policy; this doc explains pointers/references to those artifacts.

Who should read this:
- Security engineers and compliance owners responsible for evidence packaging and retention
- SRE/oncall engineers tasked with incident evidence collection
- Product and legal stakeholders requesting certified evidence for audits

Definitions:
- Evidence Bundle: a tamper-evident, time-stamped package containing authorization decision logs, entitlement diffs, audit context, and a manifest that references any large payloads (e.g., S3/GCS blobs).
- Warranty Window: the time period during which Redwood guarantees evidence availability and integrity as specified by the SLA.
- Fusion: deterministic correlation of auth events, audit events, and service identity traces into the Evidence Bundle.

Principles:
- Minimality: bundle only the artifacts required to prove a claim; large payloads referenced as immutable pointers.
- Non-repudiation: all bundles are signed and hashed with KMS-backed keys.
- Observability-first: each fusion step emits telemetry to the evidence-orchestrator metric stream.
- Timebound guarantees: warranty metadata must include value-level SLOs and expiration.

Process overview (high level):
1) Trigger detection
   - Triggers: policy exception, high-risk entitlement change, incident declaration, or regulatory evidence request.
2) Evidence collection
   - Auth logs: authz-decisions stream (service: authz-audit-producer)
   - Entitlement changes: entitlement-store changelog (service: entitlement-writer)
   - Audit context: immutable-audit-store entries including request headers, caller identity, region tags
3) Fusion and packaging
   - Evidence Orchestrator correlates by request_id, session_id, and event timestamps
   - Generates a manifest.json and computes SHA256 hashes for each referenced artifact
4) Warranty issuance
   - Evidence bundle signed by evidence-orchestrator using KMS key alias: alias/evidence-warranty
   - Warranty metadata recorded in warranty-index (searchable)
5) Retention and access
   - Bundles stored in evidence-escrow-bucket with lifecycle and retention policies
   - Access governed by just-in-time access tokens and short lived presigned URLs

Detailed workflow (step-by-step)

Step 0 — Preconditions\- Owner: security-evidence@redwood (primary)\- Required services: authz-audit-producer, entitlement-writer, evidence-orchestrator, immutable-audit-store, warranty-index, kms-hsm\- Minimum telemetry retention: 90 days in hot indices; 2 years in cold archive per data-residency policy (see related pages)

Step 1 — Triggering the fusion flow
- Who can trigger: security engineer, SRE oncall, legal/compliance, or automation rule.
- Manual trigger (CLI): evidencectl collect --tenant TENANT_ID --window "2025-10-15T00:00:00Z/2025-10-15T01:00:00Z" --reason "privileged-role-activation"
- Automated trigger: policy engine rule matching 'high-risk-entitlement-change' outputs a fusion job to the evidence-orchestrator queue.

Step 2 — Collecting and validating inputs
- The orchestrator fetches:
  - authz-decisions for tenant and time window (service endpoint: POST /streams/authz/lookup)
  - entitlement diffs from entitlement-store (API call: GET /entitlements/{tenant}/changes?since=...)
  - audit log slices from immutable-audit-store (Backfill allowed via signed archive pointer)
- Validation checks: schema conformance, timestamp monotonicity, identity resolution success. Failure to validate moves job to 'inspection' state and notifies the owner.

Step 3 — Correlation heuristics and fusion rules
- Correlate by three primary keys in order: request_id, principal_id + timestamp window (±5s), session_id.
- Fuzzy-correlation rules for edge cases (edge-runtime requests, network retries): allow timestamp window ±60s and require 2/3 context match.
- Log sampling: if events exceed 500k rows, the orchestrator performs deterministic sampling and attaches proof of sampling to the manifest.

Step 4 — Manifest and hashing
- Manifest fields (example snippet):
  - manifest_version: 1
  - generated_at: 2025-10-16T12:00:00Z
  - schema_hash: sha256:...
  - artifacts: [ {"path":"s3://evidence-escrow/tenantX/2025-10-15/authz.json.gz","sha256":"..."}, ... ]
- All artifacts hashed. The manifest itself is signed with KMS and checksum recorded in warranty-index.

Step 5 — Warranty issuance and SLA commitments
- Warranty metadata includes: warranty_id, bundle_id, warranty_issued_by, warranty_issued_at, warranty_expires_at, warranty_slo_level.
- SLO tiers (evidence retrieval):
  - Platinum: 1 minute median retrieval for bundle < 1GB; 99th percentile < 5 minutes; retention 2 years.
  - Gold: 15 minute median; 99th percentile < 1 hour; retention 1 year.
  - Standard: 4 hour median; 99th percentile < 24 hours; retention 90 days.
- SLA constraints: Platinum available for Dedicated and Private customers only, requires entitlement in contract.

Storage and retention mapping (table)
- The following ASCII table maps artifact type to storage location, retention, and access control.

| Artifact Type                | Default Storage                | Retention | Access Policy                 | Evidence Tag |
|-----------------------------|-------------------------------|-----------|------------------------------|--------------|
| Authz decisions (raw)       | immutable-audit-store (hot)   | 90d/2y    | restricted-read (security)   | authz-raw    |
| Entitlement diffs           | entitlement-archive (cold)    | 365d      | restricted-read (security)   | ent-diff     |
| Request payload pointers    | evidence-escrow (blob refs)   | per-policy| presigned + JIT role grant   | payload-ref  |
| Signed manifest             | warranty-index + escrow       | 2y        | read-only (warranty-index)   | manifest     |
| Forensic artifact bundle    | evidence-escrow (immutable)   | per-warranty | restricted-evidence-access | bundle       |

Exception and risk treatment matrix
- Low risk: evidence fusion succeeds and warranty issued automatically.
- Medium risk: partial validation failures (schema mismatch) — requires two-party signoff (security + SRE) and ticketing in JIRA.
- High risk: missing critical events or suspected tampering — escalate to Incident Response and Legal; preserve raw storage immediate snapshot; escalate to executive compliance lead.

Forensic containment checklist (run-forensic)
1) Freeze retention: evidencectl freeze-bucket --bucket evidence-escrow --reason "incident-<ID>"
2) Snapshot indices: curl -XPOST https://immutable-audit-store/_snapshot ...
3) Rotate KMS signing key for new bundles (optional escalation): aws kms schedule-key-deletion --key-id alias/evidence-warranty --pending-window-in-days 7
4) Log all access requests and append to warranty-index audit trail.

Automation patterns and example commands
- Create bundle (automation):
  - evidencectl create-bundle --tenant T-123 --from "2025-10-15T00:00Z" --to "2025-10-15T01:00Z" --slo gold
- Retrieve bundle:
  - evidencectl retrieve --bundle B-20251015-001 --presigned --format tar.gz
- Verify manifest signature (local):
  - curl -s https://warranty-index/api/bundle/B-.../manifest | jq -r '.signature' | openssl dgst -sha256 -verify public.pem -signature - manifest.json

Access and approval workflow
- Standard requests: open ticket in SECURITY-EVIDENCE queue, include tenant_id, window, and justification. Security team performs triage within 24 hours.
- Emergency (incident) requests: mark P0 and notify security-oncall; evidence-orchestrator prioritizes fusion jobs and tags them with 'incident' level processing.

Exception handling and appeals
- If warranty cannot be issued the requester receives an Evidence Rejection Report with: missing_artifacts, validation_errors, remediation_steps, and suggested compensating controls.
- Appeals path: compliance@redwood escalates to Security Director and Evidence Council for review within 5 business days.

Ownership, roles and contact matrix
- Evidence Owner (primary): security-evidence@redwood (team)
- Oncall (first response): security-oncall (PagerDuty)
- Long-term custody: infra-storage@redwood
- Legal/Compliance contact: legal-compliance@redwood

Operational metrics and alerts
- Key metrics emitted by evidence-orchestrator: fusion_success_rate, median_bundle_generation_ms, manifest_sign_failures, warranty_issuance_latency.
- Alerts:
  - fusion_success_rate < 98% (5m window) -> page security-oncall
  - manifest_sign_failures > 0 (1m) -> pager and ticket
  - evidence-escrow low-storage (<10% free) -> page infra-storage

Audit and review cadence
- Quarterly audit: reconcile warranty-index entries with contract obligations and retention schedules.
- Monthly tabletop: run simulated evidence requests for one random tenant and validate retrieval time under each SLO tier.

Appendix A — Sample manifest snippet (human readable)
{\n  \"bundle_id\": \"B-20251015-001\",\n  \"generated_at\": \"2025-10-16T12:00:00Z\",\n  \"artifacts\": [\n    {\"name\": \"authz.json.gz\", \"path\": \"s3://evidence-escrow/tenantX/B-.../authz.json.gz\", \"sha256\": \"...\"},\n    {\"name\": \"ent-diff.ndjson\", \"path\": \"s3://entitlement-archive/...\", \"sha256\": \"...\"}\n  ],\n  \"warranty\": {\"warranty_id\": \"W-20251016-01\", \"issued_by\": \"evidence-orchestrator@redwood\", \"expires_at\": \"2027-10-16T12:00:00Z\"}\n}
